text:
The Penguins went into Saturday with their own stars in the trade headlines. Pierre LeBrun has reported Carolina's interest in Erik Karlsson, there is chatter about Evgeni Malkin, and TribLIVE's Mark Madden asked whether "the unthinkable" was now thinkable for Sidney Crosby. They led after one period. Then Ottawa scored four straight and won 4-1.

Pittsburgh had the better of the first (0.97 expected goals to 0.44), and Tommy Novak scored with eight seconds left in it, from Egor Chinakhov and Ben Kindel. From there it was the Senators. Michael Amadio tied it on his own at 8:41 of the second, and Claude Giroux, still going at 38, scored on a backhand at 16:12 off an Amadio pass. That was the goal that swung it, Ottawa's win chance moving from 48% to 71%. Tim Stützle added a goal in the third on a 5% chance, and Thomas Chabot scored late to close it.

Shots finished 34-17 for Ottawa, and the third period was one-way traffic (1.18 expected goals to 0.30). Linus Ullmark only had to face 17 shots and stopped 16, 1.2 goals better than those shots usually allow. Sergei Murashov was fine at the other end, 30 saves on 33, and his best stop on Stützle in the second kept it level for a while. Rickard Rakell missed the net on Pittsburgh's best chance, a 24% look.

On chances it was closer than the score: the Senators won this game in 56% of our replays. Amadio, who just hired a new agent ahead of extension talks per the Ottawa Citizen, was the first star. The Senators also beat Colorado in overtime on Thursday, all while dealing with the loss of Nick Cousins after Jakob Chychrun's hit. For Pittsburgh, the trade talk will only get louder.
headline: Ottawa takes over after one, and Pittsburgh's week gets worse
